title: Healthcare’s Agent Bytecode: X12 as the Harness for AI Agents — Vasant Kearney, Onlay
talk_summary: The speaker argues that healthcare agents need a harness of strict schemas/contracts like X12, scoped memory, permissions, checks, and evals around the model. He recommends balancing free agent reasoning with hardcoded guardrails, preserving context, and using cheap models skeptically with regression testing before swaps.

takeaways.what_they_do: Before changing routed models, rerun task-specific evals and validation because a higher-scoring model can still break the surrounding harness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't just replace the model and assume it's going to be better

takeaways.what_they_do: Ground agent actions in typed, public contracts and reject invalid outputs at each step so errors do not propagate through long chains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: x12 is exactly this so it provides this underlying structure this contract

takeaways.what_they_do: Use deterministic code for repeatable steps and reserve agentic reasoning for ambiguous parts to avoid both error propagation and code bloat.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what we want to do is strike this balance

takeaways.technique: Preserve raw context alongside extracted findings
takeaways.what_they_do: Lossy extraction can miss downstream-relevant details, so keep original artifacts available when combining with other data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it might be that you're extracting all this information and missing something

takeaways.what_they_do: Use small or cheap models conservatively for high-volume routine tasks and avoid overpowered models when cost dominates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't want to use an overpowered over expensive model

takeaways.what_they_do: Use partner, org, and user memory to infer recurring intent, but avoid persistent bias and let users break out.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to make sure that the use any user can break out of this.
